variants.name: Reservation ledger
variants.summary: Service level: how Inventory service sets stock aside for an order and keeps its counts true.

nodes.responsibility: Shows each product page with how many are left

nodes.name: Checkout API
nodes.responsibility: Takes an order, charges it and confirms it

nodes.name: Stock API
nodes.responsibility: The HTTP routes other services call

nodes.name: Availability route
nodes.responsibility: GET /stock/{product}: how many can still be sold

nodes.name: Reserve route
nodes.responsibility: POST /reservations: sets an order's items aside

nodes.name: Release route
nodes.responsibility: DELETE /reservations/{order}: puts a cancelled order's items back

nodes.name: Reservation ledger
nodes.responsibility: Sets items aside only while enough are left
nodes.description: Locks each item's row, compares the count with what is already reserved, and writes the reservation in the same transaction. The only part that changes a reservation.

nodes.name: Stock DB
nodes.responsibility: Each product's count and its reservations

nodes.name: Warehouse sync

nodes.name: Warehouse system
nodes.responsibility: What the warehouse says is on its shelves

edges.label: lock, check and reserve in one transaction

flows.name: Reserve an order's items
flows.summary: One reservation, from Checkout API's request to its answer.

steps.label: lock each item's row
steps.note: a second order for the same item waits here until the first commits

steps.label: check every item is covered
steps.note: one item short: nothing is reserved and the answer is 409 sold out

beats.heading: Checkout reserves the items before it charges the card
beats.body: When a shopper presses Pay, Checkout API sends the order's items to Reserve route and waits for the answer. It charges the card only once the items are set aside.

beats.heading: Only the ledger sets items aside
beats.body: Reservation ledger locks each item's row in Stock DB, checks that the count minus what is already reserved covers the order, and writes the reservation in the same transaction.

beats.heading: The last item goes to the first order
beats.body: Two shoppers can press Pay for the last item at the same moment. The row lock makes the second order wait for the first; it then finds nothing left, gets 409 sold out, and that shopper is told the item has sold out.

beats.heading: A cancelled order puts its items back
beats.body: When checkout cancels an order, Checkout API calls Release route and the ledger deletes that order's reservations. Nothing else gives reserved items back, so an order checkout forgets to cancel keeps its items.

beats.heading: The counts come from the warehouse
beats.body: Every 5 minutes Warehouse sync reads what the warehouse has on its shelves and sets each count in Stock DB. Reservations are subtracted from that count, never written into it.

beats.heading: Reserved means nobody else can buy it
beats.body: When checkout reserves an order's items, Inventory service sets them aside so nobody else can buy them, and puts them back when the order is cancelled. The counts it starts from are never more than 5 minutes old.
